data.why: A muddy puddle on a plain lawn in section in front, a battery and bulb beside it, and the chip line behind (furnace with a carbon bin, crystal puller, wafer table, light printer) that a hall closes around later. The story follows the sand: furnace, silicon, crystal, wafer, printer, chip; each fix brings the next problem, and the bulb that stayed dark on sand glows on the finished chip over the clear puddle. The camera opens close on the puddle and frames each machine as it works.

ideas.idea: a muddy puddle that settles leaves a bed of sand
sand is silicon bound to oxygen and carries no current
the sand goes into a furnace with carbon
cold, the oxygen stays bound to the silicon
electric arcs heat it so hot the carbon takes the oxygen away as gas
the silicon comes out as a jumble of many small crystals
it is melted and one single crystal is pulled from it
the single crystal is a big heavy log
a wire saw cuts it into thin wafers
the saw leaves the wafers scratched
polishing makes each wafer a perfect mirror
a plain mirror of silicon does nothing yet
a printer uses light through a mask to draw switches on the wafer
a single speck of dust in the light spoils a chip
a hall with filtered air blowing down keeps the dust out
this is a cleanroom
the switches stand alone with no wiring between them
layers of copper wiring join them up
a few of the wires are faulty and some chips fail
every chip is tested and the bad ones are marked
a good chip is a bare sliver with nothing to plug into
it is sealed in a black case with metal legs
the chip plugs in and the bulb glows over the clear puddle
you have built a chip factory

chain.shows: a battery and bulb in the sand stay dark
chain.stakes: nothing can be made from it

chain.shows: the cold furnace full of sand and carbon does nothing
the silicon pours out as a jumble of grey lumps
chain.stakes: electrons trip at every crystal edge

chain.shows: the pulled crystal hangs as a heavy log
chain.stakes: it is far too thick for a chip

chain.shows: the saw leaves the wafers scratched
chain.stakes: no pattern can be printed on them

chain.shows: the polished wafers are bare and empty
dust specks fall in the printer's light onto the wafer
the printed switches sit apart with nothing joining them
sparks fly from faulty copper wires
a good chip is a bare sliver with nothing to plug into
chain.stakes: it cannot be used in anything

surprises.claim: Silicon is made by heating quartz sand with carbon in an electric arc furnace at up to about 2,000 degrees Celsius
surprises.search: metallurgical silicon arc furnace quartz carbon 2000 C

surprises.claim: Chips are made from one single silicon crystal pulled slowly from melted silicon (the Czochralski method)
surprises.search: Czochralski process single crystal silicon ingot pulled from melt

surprises.claim: Cleanrooms for chips blow filtered air down from the ceiling to keep dust off the wafers
surprises.search: semiconductor cleanroom HEPA filtered laminar airflow ceiling down

sentences.text: If you let a muddy puddle settle, you have sand.
But sand is silicon locked to oxygen, so the bulb stays dark.
So you shovel the sand into a furnace with carbon.
But in a cold furnace, the oxygen stays locked on.
So electric arcs heat it to about 2,000 degrees.
But the silicon pours out as a jumble of crystals.
So you melt it and pull out one single crystal.
But that crystal is a heavy log, far too thick.
So a wire saw slices it into thin wafers.
But the saw leaves every wafer scratched and rough.
So you polish each wafer into a mirror.
But a bare silicon mirror does nothing on its own.
So a printer shines light through a mask, drawing switches.
But one speck of dust in that light ruins the chip.
So you build a hall and blow filtered air down.
This is a cleanroom.
But even in the hall, the printed switches sit unconnected.
So you lay thin copper wires over them in layers.
But a few copper wires short out, and some chips fail.
So you test every chip and mark the bad ones.
But good chips are bare slivers with nothing to plug in.
So you seal each in a black case with legs.
Plug one in, and the bulb glows over the clear puddle.
Congratulations, you have built a chip factory.
